messages.text:
[redacted:local-path] Infinite Labyrinth I need you to evaluate the codebase and tell me where I am going wrong in both the realtime action roguelike/looter-shooter gameplay as well as the Menu/UI/Graphics/Art because the game is technically sound but looks and feels bad and it is difficult to explain to the AI agent in VS Code, there is a fundamental disconnect in communication.
I need you to come up with a research plan for improving my game.

Apocky, this is a great request — and I think the "communication disconnect" is probably the most important problem to solve here. A few quick questions so I can make this research razor-sharp:

Once you answer these I'll dive deep into research on game feel frameworks, SDF visual polish techniques, and — critically — how to bridge the communication gap so you can actually direct an AI agent to implement "feel" improvements systematically rather than just syntactically.

Q: When you say it 'feels bad' — what's the primary sensation? (This helps me target the right research domain) (Select all that apply)
A: Input feels laggy/unresponsive, Animations are stiff/robotic, No juice (screenshake, particles, hit feedback), Camera feels wrong, Movement/physics feel floaty or rigid

Q: For the visual side — where's the biggest gap between intent and result? (Select all that apply)
A: SDF rendering looks too 'tech demo', Colors/palette feel flat or wrong, UI/menus look programmer-art, No visual hierarchy or readability

Q: What's the core communication disconnect with the AI agent in VS Code?
A: It doesn't know what good game feel looks like

You picked *everything* — which actually tells me a lot. This isn't a "fix one thing" situation, it's a foundational game feel and visual direction problem. And the fact that the AI agent "doesn't know what good game feel looks like" is the root cause — you can't direct implementation of something the tool has no mental model for.

Let me do a deep research dive. I'm going to focus on actionable frameworks you can use both to improve the game *and* to bridge that communication gap with your AI agent.

Your game feel improvement plan for SDF roguelikes is ready. It covers a prioritized juice implementation stack (hitstop, screenshake, hit flash), specific numerical parameters for movement tuning, procedural animation techniques using Disney's 12 principles, SDF shader recipes for transforming math shapes into art, UI architecture with MSDF font rendering, and a complete workflow for directing AI coding agents using config-driven development. The report includes implementation-ready values drawn from Dead Cells, Hollow Knight, Hades, Nuclear Throne, and Noita, along with a 9-week development roadmap.
